reader.requirement: START sets the key of reference to (a) the prime key when the KEY phrase is omitted, (b) the named record key, or (c) the record key that shares the operand's leftmost position (any alphanumeric item in a record of the file, no longer than the key). It uses that key for the comparison and, on success, for later sequential READs; on failure there is no valid next record.

reader.notes: BindStart picks keyIndex from KeyIndexOfKeyItem or GenericKeyIndex, or the prime key when KEY is omitted. Start/StartSucceeded make it _refKey for later READ NEXT. The SR6 message cites 2023's 'same class, category and usage'; at 1985 every key is alphanumeric DISPLAY, so it accepts and refuses the same operands as SR4b.

refuter.evidence: q6_start_ops.cob (--std 85, sequential access, READ without NEXT) used a group alternate key (99 + X) holding a numeric subordinate. All seven spellings of the 1985 format were accepted and walked by the alternate key: = 10D -> 04,03,01; GREATER/> 10D -> 03,01; NOT LESS/NOT </GREATER OR EQUAL/>= 20C -> 03,01. A one-character generic key in a second 01 (FILLER redefinition at the alternate's leftmost position) behaved under GR10c: =2 -> 03,01; =3 -> 01; =1 -> 02,04,03,01; =4 -> 23, then READ -> 46 (GR8). q4_pcs.cob: the comparisons use the native collating sequence under a reversed PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (§1985:B.2.2). §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR4 forbids two keys sharing a leftmost position, so GR10c always picks one key. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR10; OK §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR4; OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR8.
